items.question_text: A GP sees a well 40-year-old for a 6-minute chat about a holiday. No history, examination, or management is recorded. The receptionist asks which Medicare item to bill. What is the most appropriate action?  No symptom was assessed. No examination. No plan. Billing any attendance item would be a false claim. Do not bill. That is the correct step.  Nothing in the history creates an exception for billing, access, or a rural workaround. The standard is the same.  Decide on the rule, not on what would be easier to claim or to arrange tonight.  That settles the item.

Bill a level B. Any attendance can be claimed
Bill a health assessment. He is an adult
